reasons: The test was not run while writing these notes.
It checks real behaviour across several steps, so it is strong evidence once it passes.

terms.meaning: A tool that controls a real web browser from code, so a test can click and read the page like a person.
The test runner that starts the tests and reports pass or fail.
A development server that serves the app while it is being tested.
An open-source web browser used by the test.
Checking that two images match, one value at a time.
A single HTML file that opens and shows the 3D view without an internet connection.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and imports
sections.what: Brings in the browser tools, the dev server, the test runner and the app's data types. It also declares the shared variables for the backend, server, browser and temporary folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the test needs every tool in one place before any step runs.
sections.watch_out: The backend is started with the python command, so a machine where that command is missing will fail at startup.

sections.name: required
sections.title: Starting and stopping test services
sections.what: Starts the Python backend on a free port, waits for it to report that port, then starts the dev server with a small probe that records what the 3D view draws. It also launches Chromium before the tests and closes everything afterwards.
sections.why: Likely reason: each run needs fresh services and must clean up so later runs are not affected.
sections.watch_out: The probe looks for an exact line of code in SceneView. If that line changes, the setup fails with a message about the marker.

sections.name: endDate (part 1)
sections.title: Schedule slider helper and the main test start
sections.what: The helper moves the schedule slider to its last date by pressing Home then End. The main test begins by uploading a small schedule, waiting until it is ready, and reading the first component.
sections.why: Likely reason: moving to the end date makes the 3D view show every part, which the checks rely on.
sections.watch_out: The helper depends on the slider's accessible name, so renaming that label breaks the test.

sections.name: endDate (part 2)
sections.title: Editing, saving and template steps
sections.what: Changes recipe sizes and positions, adds a cylinder and a box, removes a recipe, and saves. It then checks the saved data against the edits, creates, edits, assigns and deletes a template, and reloads the page to confirm the 3D view shows three parts.
sections.why: Likely reason: covers each main editor action in one sequence to catch problems between steps.
sections.watch_out: Checks a specific colour code for one part, so changing that colour will fail the test even if the shape is correct.

sections.name: endDate (part 3)
sections.title: Offline export and picture comparison
sections.what: Downloads the offline HTML file, opens it with no server, and checks that it made no outside requests and produced no page errors. It then compares the live and offline pictures and fails if more than 1 percent of colour values differ by a noticeable amount.
sections.why: Likely reason: an exported file must look the same as the live view, and must not depend on the internet.
sections.watch_out: Picture comparisons can differ slightly between computers, which may cause false failures.

summary: An automated browser test that saves a component's custom shape recipes and templates, reopens them, and checks that the live and offline 3D views match.
purpose: Proves the assembly editor works end to end on real data, not only in isolation.
why: Likely reason: the editor touches the saved model, the 3D view and the offline export, so only a full run can catch a break between them.
how: Starts a synthetic Python backend and a development server, opens the app in Chromium, uploads a small schedule, edits recipes, saves, creates, edits, assigns and deletes a template, reloads, then exports an offline HTML file and compares its picture with the live view.
inputs: A synthetic CSV schedule written inside the test, the Python test server in tests/assembly_browser_server.py, and a local Chromium browser.
outputs: Pass or fail results. Temporary folders are removed at the end of the run.
risks: Slow, with the main test allowed up to two minutes. Needs Python and Chromium on the machine. Uses exact button labels and a fixed colour code, so UI text changes can break it.
debug: If the backend does not start, check the Python setup and the port message. If the picture comparison fails, compare the two saved screenshots first. If a label is not found, search for that label text in AssemblyEditor.tsx.
